card.name: Period after abbreviated names and citations
card.fires_on: The period right after a shortened word or initial in references, such as an author initial, journal abbreviation, or classical source title. The next word is usually a name or citation detail.

modes.label: Journal and author citations
modes.description: Period after an author initial or journal abbreviation in a reference list.
modes.example: 2. Fratzl, P<<.>> and R. Weinkamer, Nature

modes.label: Classical source abbreviations
modes.description: Period after a cut-down ancient author or work title in footnotes.

modes.label: Abbreviated names and dates in prose
modes.description: Period after a shortened place, first name, or weekday in ordinary text.
modes.example: Then they went to Sault Ste<<.>> Marie, Mackinac and Petos

card.writes: It seems to push toward a name or title continuing after the abbreviation, such as 'eldon' or 'Station', and away from word endings.
card.plain: It marks the dot after an abbreviated name or source in a reference, where the full name or citation continues.
